summary.title: Are We Ready For An Agent-Native Memory System?

details: Agent memory for LLM agents has become a full data management system (persist, retrieve, update, consolidate, govern lifecycle), yet prior benchmarks treat it as a black box scored only by end-to-end task metrics (F1, BLEU), ignoring operational cost, module-level architectural trade-offs, and robustness under knowledge updates.

A data-management-oriented analytical framework plus experimental study that decomposes any agent memory system into four modules -- memory representation & storage, memory extraction, memory retrieval & query routing, and memory maintenance -- and builds a taxonomy of existing systems along these axes.

Evaluation crux: instead of only end-to-end scores, systems are compared on multi-dimensional axes (task effectiveness, evidence-level retrieval fidelity, dynamic update robustness, long-horizon stability, operational cost) and then dissected by controlled one-module-at-a-time variants of real systems.

12 representative memory systems grouped as sequential-context (MemoChat, Mem0, MEM1, MemAgent), structural-topological (MemTree, Zep, Mem0^g, Cognee), and multi-paradigm hybrid (LightMem, SimpleMem, MemOS, MemoryOS, A-MEM, Letta/MemGPT).
Two reference baselines: Long Context (dump history into prompt) and Embedding RAG (flat dense retrieval).

Five benchmark workloads spanning 11 datasets; main ones: LoCoMo (long-conversation episodic/temporal/multi-hop QA), LongMemEval via MemoryAgentBench (multi-session, knowledge-update and temporal-reasoning slices), DB-Bench from LifelongAgentBench (procedural DB task execution), LongBench (controlled short/medium/long context buckets).

Metrics: Exact Match, Answer F1, Substring EM, ROUGE-L F1/Recall, GPT-5.4-based LLM-judge accuracy, task success rate; Recall@K over gold source-level evidence; Recall@10 and F1 binned by evidence-distance gap (1-5 up to 26-31 sessions) and by session-history count.

Unified time-overhead traces from a common runner for 8 systems: average operation latency per query (construction + query time, amortized) vs. min-max normalized utility averaged over six answer-quality metrics; outlier-filtered average total latency per query across three benchmarks.
M1 representation: LightMem User-Only Raw vs. Summary vs. Compressed; MemTree flat-biased vs. deeper tree; Mem0 default vector vs. graph store.
M2 extraction: MemoChat heuristic vs. LLM topic segmentation; MemOS Fast vs. Fine Memorize on the same tree_text backend; LightMem user-only vs. hybrid (user+assistant) raw.
M3 retrieval/routing: A-MEM hybrid-balanced vs. sparse-leaning fusion; SimpleMem no planning vs. planning-only vs. planning+reflect.
M4 maintenance: MemoChat multi-topic vs. forced single-topic summaries; MemoryOS default vs. delayed-flush vs. conservative-merge.
Backbone robustness: 6 memory settings under 4 LLM backbones (including GPT-5.4-mini and GPT-5.4) on LoCoMo.

key_findings.finding: No memory architecture dominates; effectiveness is determined by how well the memory structure matches the dominant workload bottleneck.
key_findings.evidence: Across workloads the leader shifts: Zep reaches 48.0 LLM-judge accuracy and Cognee 35.3 ROUGE-L F1 on LongMemEval; MemOS gets the best LoCoMo EM (11.5); on DB-Bench Long Context is best on EM (48.20) while MemoChat attains the highest task success rate (55.40). MemoryOS and MemOS are closest to the frontier across all workloads.

key_findings.finding: Structured, linked or hierarchical memory sustains retrieval fidelity and long-horizon stability, whereas flat dense retrieval and raw long context degrade sharply with temporal distance or context length.
key_findings.evidence: On LoCoMo retrieval, SimpleMem leads Recall@1 (39.0) but A-MEM (69.5/85.9 Recall@5/@10) and MemTree (59.7/80.5) dominate at larger budgets and stay stable across evidence-gap bins, while Embedding RAG collapses (Answer F1 37.1 to 7.4 as gap widens). On LongBench, SimpleMem holds 35.2 to 34.9 accuracy from short to medium buckets while Long Context falls 42.6 to 19.0.

key_findings.finding: Graph- and relation-organized memory handles knowledge revision and temporal state most reliably, while fact-extraction plugins and append-only/flat stores return stale facts.
key_findings.evidence: On LongMemEval Knowledge Update, Zep leads with 44.4 Substring EM / 36.8 ROUGE-L F1 and Cognee leads Temporal Reasoning (18.7 / 35.8), versus Mem0 (15.6 / 17.1), SimpleMem (6.7 / 7.4) and Letta (17.8 / 5.7); on LoCoMo Temporal, MemOS is best on EM (8.9) and Cognee on Answer F1 (28.1).

key_findings.finding: Operational efficiency is governed by how far each write propagates (maintenance scope), and high-cost structured systems do not deliver proportional accuracy.
key_findings.evidence: LightMem reaches 48.3 normalized utility at 3.67 s/query and MemTree 63.5 at 15.9 s, while Cognee and Zep exceed 84 utility only at 116.5 s and 155.1 s; on LongBench per-query latency, LightMem stays at 17.3 s while MemoryOS and A-MEM rise to 490.0 s and 552.1 s.

key_findings.finding: Each abstraction layer discards information: raw retention beats summarization/compression, coverage-preserving extraction beats aggressive filtering, and conservative consolidation is the best default maintenance policy.
key_findings.evidence: LightMem User-Only Raw is best on all four metrics (e.g., 26.0 Substring EM on LongMemEval vs. 10.7 compressed and 11.7 summary); MemOS Fine Memorize collapses on LoCoMo multi-hop (2.5 EM / 5.0 F1 vs. 25.5 / 40.8 for Fast Memorize) despite small LongMemEval gains; MemoryOS Conservative-Merge improves to 23.5 Ans. F1 / 22.8 Substr. EM over default 23.2/22.4 while Delayed-Flush drops to 20.6/19.5; SimpleMem Planning-Only (20.7 F1, 90.6 recall) beats both no-planning and planning+reflect.
